findings.evidence: "Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Write a sentence specific to each paragraph's actual request instead of reusing the same boilerplate line.
findings.violation: This generic sentence is reused verbatim across unrelated paragraphs (s1-p1, s1-p2, s2-p1) no matter what "the same request" actually refers to, making the referent unclear and the content feel templated.

findings.evidence: "Commuters can report a service issue by calling rider services. Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate sentence or rewrite it so it isn't identical across paragraphs.
findings.violation: This is a verbatim duplicate of the closing sentence already used in s1-p1.

findings.evidence: alt="Crews repainting the accessible parking spaces near the station entrance." on src="/img/platform-update.jpg"
findings.fix: Confirm the correct image for this section and make the filename, alt text, and surrounding content consistent.
findings.violation: The alt text describes parking-lot repainting while the filename and the "Station updates" section imply a platform/schedule update, so the image content doesn't match its context.

findings.evidence: Heading "Schedule changes" followed by a table reading "North / On time", "South / On time"
findings.fix: Rename the heading to reflect current status (e.g., "Zone status") or add content that actually documents schedule changes.
findings.violation: The heading promises information about schedule changes, but the table only reports current on-time status with no change shown.

findings.evidence: "Passengers can check real time arrivals through the online portal. Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Deduplicate across the document; write context-appropriate text or drop the sentence.
findings.violation: This is the third verbatim repetition of the same "same request" boilerplate sentence (also in s1-p1 and s1-p2).

findings.evidence: "Riders can report a service issue by calling rider services. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day."
findings.fix: Replace the second sentence with information relevant to reporting an issue, such as expected response time.
findings.violation: The second sentence (about updates posting to a schedule page) doesn't logically follow from the first sentence about reporting an issue by phone; the two look like mismatched boilerplate stitched together.

findings.evidence: "Local residents can check real time arrivals through the online portal. A confirmation message follows once the request is processed."
findings.fix: Remove or replace the second sentence with text relevant to checking arrivals, such as portal refresh frequency.
findings.violation: Checking real-time arrivals isn't a submitted request that gets "processed," so the second sentence doesn't match the first.

findings.evidence: "Route adjustments take effect on the posted effective date."
findings.fix: State the actual effective date or timeframe, or remove the banner.
findings.violation: This is a tautology (an "effective date" is by definition when something takes effect) and conveys no actual information.

findings.evidence: "Riders can check real time arrivals at any station kiosk. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day."
findings.fix: Write status-card text specific to what the adjacent "Refresh status" button actually does, removing the conflicting boilerplate.
findings.violation: This reuses the mismatched "within one business day" boilerplate from s3-p1 and sits directly above a "Refresh status" button, creating a contradiction between an instant manual refresh and a one-business-day update delay.

findings.fix: Wrap the status content in an `aria-live="polite"` region that updates when the button is activated.
findings.violation: The button presumably updates the status card dynamically, but there is no aria-live region or other mechanism to announce the updated status to screen reader users.

findings.fix: Replace the div with a real `<button>` element, and remove this control if it is leftover from another page/template since it has no apparent purpose here.
findings.violation: A "Delete item" control appears on a route-updates/fare-adjustments page with no list of deletable items for context, and it's built from a div with role="button" instead of a native button element, an accessibility anti-pattern.

findings.evidence: "Choose a plan" / "Enter payment details" / "Confirm your order"
findings.fix: Remove the wizard-steps block from this page or replace it with steps actually relevant to fare adjustments.
findings.violation: These checkout-wizard steps are unrelated to fare adjustments or route updates and appear to be a misplaced component from a different flow.

findings.evidence: "For the full list of upcoming adjustments, read the accessibility improvements list" (href="/fares/history")
findings.fix: Change the link text to accurately describe the destination, e.g., "read the full list of fare adjustments."
findings.violation: The link text "read the accessibility improvements list" doesn't match the preceding text about "upcoming adjustments" or the destination URL "/fares/history," so the link is mislabeled.

findings.evidence: `<label for="phone" ...>Phone number (required)</label>` paired with `<input id="phone" type="tel">`
findings.fix: Add `required` and/or `aria-required="true"` to the phone input.
findings.violation: The label states the field is required, but the input has no `required` or `aria-required="true"` attribute, so this isn't enforced or conveyed to assistive technology.

findings.evidence: `` followed by `Enter a 6 character code using letters and numbers only.`
findings.fix: Set `aria-invalid` dynamically based on real validation state and add `aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error"` to the input.
findings.violation: `aria-invalid` is hardcoded to "true" regardless of actual input state, and the error text isn't linked to the input via `aria-describedby`, so screen reader users hear a false "invalid" announcement with no explanation.
